turns.t: Mr Lindsay, I'm Una, the nurse, and I've got your tablet list ready for the doctor. Your carer's welcome to sit in. ~
Thank you. I'm Denise, I look after Mr Lindsay on weekday mornings. ~
Good morning. I should say that I'd like this to be accurate, so I shall be precise. ~
That suits me, Mr Lindsay. What brings you in? ~
Last Tuesday, at 10.40 in the morning, I lost the vision in my left eye. Completely, like a curtain coming down from above. It lasted about four minutes, and then it went away.
That's very clear, thank you. Was it just the one eye?
Yes. When I covered the right eye, I could see nothing. When I covered the left, the right was normal.
He phoned me straight away. I think he was shaken. ~
Has it happened before or since? ~
Not before. Not since. ~
Any pain in the eye, headache, or flashing lights?
No pain. No headache. No flashes.
Any weakness in your face or limbs, or any trouble with speech at that time?
None of those.
Let me look at your medicines.
I've got the list, doctor. Aspirin, 75 mg, once a day. Atorvastatin, 40 mg at night. And amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day.
That is correct. ~
And your medical history?
High blood pressure, high cholesterol, and he had a heart attack, six years ago.
Let me check your eyes and your neck. Look straight ahead. ~
Of course.
Your vision, pupils and eye movements are normal, and the back of the eye looks healthy. There's a swishing sound, a bruit, over the left side of your neck.
What does that signify? ~

It can mean the artery in the neck is narrowed. Together with what you describe, a brief curtain across one eye, this is typical of a temporary blockage of the blood supply to the eye, from a narrowed neck artery. ~
A mini-stroke? ~
Of the eye, yes, it's the same process. It's a warning. I'd like you to have an urgent ultrasound scan of the arteries in your neck, a carotid scan, within days, and blood tests.
Is that a priority? ~
Yes, it needs to be done quickly. I'll arrange it as urgent, and the vascular team will see you. ~
I'll book the scan for the earliest slot, doctor. ~
Thank you, Una. Keep taking all your tablets, especially the aspirin and the atorvastatin.
I never miss them. ~
If it happens again, or you get weakness in the face or an arm, slurred speech, or loss of vision that doesn't clear, call 999 immediately.
I'll make sure he knows. ~
Thank you. I appreciate your clarity. ~
